#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   -c 4
#   -t 6:00:00
#   -p gpu
#   --gres=gpu:teslaK80:2
#   -o nv_%j.out
#   -e nv_%j.err

#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 4
#flux: --time-limit=6h

# Omitted Slurm option: --gres=gpu:teslaK80:2
# Flux GPU requests/type constraints are site/config dependent (often via custom resource types).
# Performance implication: job may start without GPUs (or without K80s / fewer than 2), causing failure or severe slowdown.

# Omitted Slurm option: -p gpu (partition)
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run on non-GPU nodes or have different limits/priority (or be rejected by policy).

# Omitted Slurm options: -o/-e with %j token
# Slurm's %j token (job id) is not portable in Flux output/error directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose unique filenames.

module load gcc/6.2.0
module load cuda/10.0

echo "#---------"
echo $CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES
nvidia-smi
nvidia-smi | grep "|\    [$CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES] " | awk '{print $3}' | xargs -r ps -o pid,ppid,uid -p
echo "#----------"

~/nvida_samples/1_Utilities/deviceQuery/deviceQuery

reasons: The original Slurm job required 2 Tesla K80 GPUs (`--gres=gpu:teslaK80:2`) but the Flux resource section does not request any GPU resources; on GPU-managed systems this may allocate CPU-only resources and the job may fail or run much slower.

The original Slurm job specified a GPU partition (`-p gpu`) but the Flux resource section has no queue/partition selection; on sites where this affects eligibility/limits, scheduling behavior may differ or the job may be rejected.
issues: The path `~/nvida_samples/...` appears misspelled (likely `nvidia_samples`), which may cause a runtime failure.
